newsitem.title: USA: Burmese group files suit against Unocal.
newsitem.headline: Burmese group files suit against Unocal.

text.p: A self-described Burmese government-in-exile filed a suit in U.S. federal court on Tuesday against Unocal Corp., a partner in the largest foreign investment project in the South Asian nation.

In a 14-page complaint the plantiffs charged the Los Angeles-based oil and gas company with human rights violations in the venture, a $1.2 billion gas pipeline it owns with France's Total oil group, Burma's state-owned Myanmar Oil & Gas Enterprise and Thailand's PTT.
Specifically it accused the joint venture of using forced labour of tens of thousands of villagers, systematic destruction of villages in the pipeline region and other human rights atrocities.

"We are seeking an injunction against Unocal and monetary damages, which as you can imagine are enormous," said attorney Jason Adkins of the Boston-based law firm of Cristobal Bonifaz, representing the National Coalition Government of the Union of Burma (NCGUB) and Federation of Trade Unions of Burma (FTUB).
Peter Schey, an attorney for the plaintiffs in Los Angeles, said the group had not determined how much they would seek in damages.
Total and Unocal have been targets of international activist groups protesting the Burmese military government's human rights record and crackdown on democracy campaigners.
Schey said the plaintiffs did not plan to sue Total.
In a statement, Unocal denied the allegations, which it described as "political."
"The $1.2 billion natural gas project has caused none of the false and outrageous allegations," it said. "We believe that this lawsuit is motivated solely by political considerations."

The NCGUB has its principal offices in Washington. The Federation of Trade Unions of Burma is based in Bangkok, Thailand. The two groups filed the lawsuit on their own behalf and on behalf of the citizens of Burma.

The suit sought a court order halting Unocal's role in the joint venture, which is building a natural gas pipeline into Thailand. It alleged Unocal relied on the State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) -- the Burmese military regime -- for providing and maintaining all military operations in the pipeline region, severely repressing Burmese citizens.

SLORC seized power in Burma in 1988. It repressed the National League for Democracy (NLD) beginning in 1990 with thousands of arrests. The lawyers said the NLD, headed by Aung San Suu Kyi, met secretly and designated a group of elected representatives to form a government-in-exile.
